deepresearch-bench

benchmark.deepresearch-bench

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Included after actual author, separate source-verifier and adversarial AI source-content reviews of exact approved bindings. Scope means the complete relevant available source documentation/methods actually recorded, with explicit bounded/unread pages, version differences and unknown rights, payload, construction or operations retained. No experiment, settled upstream rights, or human peer review is implied.

Review depth
full source
Disposition

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

deepresearch-bench · generated: DeepResearch Bench II constructs tasks from expert-authored open-access review reports selected for information gathering, substantial synthesis and reproducibility without physical experiments or complex data-mining/model pipelines.

candidate.third11.deepresearch.article-selection.v2

  • Tasks may cover a relevant subset of a source article and must fix a temporal scope when the topic is time-sensitive.

deepresearch-bench · evaluates: The original DeepResearch Bench II paper uses Gemini 2.5 Pro with batches of fifty rubrics; the captured later creator README uses GPT-5.5 and three-way rubric labels for satisfied, unmentioned, or blocked-source-supported content.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

deepresearch-bench · documents: DeepResearch Bench II’s v1 paper acknowledges incomplete prevention of source-article leakage, possible human-annotation bias and a presentation dimension that does not yet model personalization to the user’s knowledge and preferences.

candidate.third11.deepresearch.limitations.v2

  • The source-article block and expert refinement do not establish that every score is leakage-free or that all annotators would agree.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

deepresearch-bench · human annotation: DeepResearch Bench II’s v1 paper describes LLM extraction, source-article self-evaluation, manual revision and domain-expert refinement to produce atomic, content-bearing numerical or inferential rubrics, with more than 400 human-hours of expert review.

candidate.third11.deepresearch.rubric-construction.v2

  • Self-evaluation regeneration is triggered when information-recall or analysis accuracy on the source article is below 90%; this construction check is not the benchmark’s final model score.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

deepresearch-bench · dataset size: DeepResearch Bench II’s v1 paper reports 132 tasks across 22 domains and 9,430 rubrics. The later creator README retains all 132 dataset tasks but temporarily excludes tasks 112 and 114 from official scoring, leaving 130 scored tasks.

candidate.third11.deepresearch.units-and-current-scope.v2

  • The separately captured Mercor page reports 130 briefs and 9,287 criteria. Those counts are retained at its documented evaluation scope; no task/rubric payload recount is inferred.
